followups.action: Ask the site whether a Spanish-language consent form and a qualified interpreter are available for this Spanish-only patient.
followups.why: She must understand and voluntarily sign the consent form before any study procedure, so consent in Spanish decides this.

followups.action: Request the full right heart catheterization report from last year, including mPAP and PCWP.
followups.why: PAH needs PVR ≥5 WU (she has 7), PCWP ≤15 mmHg and mPAP >20 mmHg; the last two are not recorded. The site may repeat the RHC if the report is old.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether she is postmenopausal or able to become pregnant, and if able, whether she will use highly effective contraception.
followups.why: Women who can become pregnant must agree to protocol-defined highly effective contraception.

followups.action: Ask the site whether Spanish-speaking investigators or interpreters can support all visits and procedures.
followups.why: She must be able to communicate well with investigators and understand the study procedures.

followups.action: Obtain recent pulmonary function tests with FVC % predicted, and a high-resolution CT chest if FVC is 60-70% or cannot be measured.
followups.why: FVC must be >70% predicted. If it is 60-70% or cannot be measured, HRCT must show <10% fibrosis and <10% emphysema.

followups.action: Obtain full spirometry with the FEV1/FVC ratio.
followups.why: PAH participants need an FEV1/FVC ratio >0.70.

followups.action: Find any prior VQ scan, or CTPA or pulmonary angiogram, report. If none exists, order a VQ scan.
followups.why: It must show a normal or low-probability result that is not clinically significant, which helps rule out chronic thromboembolic disease.

followups.action: Order a 12-lead ECG and record the rhythm and heart rate.
followups.why: She needs normal sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 40-100 bpm.

followups.action: Read the QTcF interval from the 12-lead ECG.
followups.why: For women, QTcF must be ≤460 msec.

followups.action: Read the QRS duration from the 12-lead ECG, with a manual overread if it is over 120 msec.
followups.why: QRS must be ≤120 msec, or confirmed on manual overread if higher.

followups.action: Measure her body weight at the clinic.
followups.why: Weight must be >50.0 kg at Screening and at Baseline. Her BMI of 27 makes this likely.

followups.action: Schedule repeat 6-minute walk tests at Screening and Day 1, and share any other recent 6MWD results.
followups.why: Both walk distances must be within 15% of each other (a third test is allowed). We only have one value, 380 m.

followups.action: Confirm with the patient and her clinician that her PAH is not linked to HIV.
followups.why: HIV-associated PAH is excluded. Her idiopathic diagnosis suggests it does not apply.

followups.action: Ask her clinician whether she has portal hypertension or liver disease linked to her PAH.
followups.why: PAH associated with portal hypertension is excluded.

followups.action: Ask whether she has had schistosomiasis or lived in an area where it is common.
followups.why: Schistosomiasis-associated PAH is excluded.

followups.action: Ask her pulmonologist whether pulmonary veno-occlusive disease or capillary hemangiomatosis has been considered or found on CT or RHC.
followups.why: Either condition excludes her.

followups.action: Order a hepatitis B surface antigen blood test, or retrieve a prior result.
followups.why: A positive HBsAg excludes her.

followups.action: Order a hepatitis C antibody test, with HCV RNA PCR if positive.
followups.why: A positive antibody excludes her unless she was treated and the RNA PCR is negative.

followups.action: Order an HIV antibody test, or retrieve a prior result.
followups.why: A positive HIV antibody excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the patient about drug or other allergies and any prior exposure to ROC-101. Ask the site for the formulation components to compare.
followups.why: Known hypersensitivity to ROC-101 or its components excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the patient and her clinician whether she has had any cancer in the past 5 years, and what type.
followups.why: Cancer within 5 years excludes her, except treated basal cell carcinoma, cervical carcinoma in situ, or ≤2 skin squamous cell carcinomas.

followups.action: Ask her clinician for a list of other significant conditions (heart, kidney, liver, lung, nerve, mental health, and others) for investigator review.
followups.why: The investigator decides whether any non-PAH disease would limit participation.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether she has joined another drug or device study in the last 4 weeks, or is in one now.
followups.why: Another investigational treatment within 4 weeks (or 5 half-lives) before Baseline excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether she has had major surgery in the last 8 weeks.
followups.why: Major surgery within 8 weeks before Day 1 excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the patient and her clinician whether any major surgery is planned during the study.
followups.why: Planned major surgery in the main study excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has ever had a heart or heart-lung transplant.
followups.why: A prior heart or heart-lung transplant excludes her.

followups.action: Ask her PH team whether she is on, or being evaluated for, a heart or lung transplant list.
followups.why: Being listed for transplant excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has ever had a lung removed (pneumonectomy).
followups.why: A prior pneumonectomy excludes her.

followups.action: Order a pregnancy test (urine or serum hCG) unless she is confirmed postmenopausal.
followups.why: Pregnancy excludes her and a negative test is required.

followups.action: Ask the patient whether she is breastfeeding.
followups.why: Breastfeeding excludes her.

followups.action: Measure sitting blood pressure at the clinic.
followups.why: Sitting systolic BP >160 mm Hg excludes her.

followups.action: Check the diastolic reading on the sitting blood pressure measurement.
followups.why: Sitting diastolic BP >100 mm Hg excludes her.

followups.action: Record systolic BP at the screening visit and at Day 1.
followups.why: Systolic BP <90 mm Hg excludes her.

followups.action: Do orthostatic blood pressure checks (lying to standing) and ask about dizziness.
followups.why: A symptomatic systolic drop of more than 20 mm Hg excludes her.

followups.action: Ask her cardiologist whether she has ever had pericardial constriction.
followups.why: Known pericardial constriction excludes her.

followups.action: Get a recent echocardiogram report, or schedule one, and check for pericardial effusion.
followups.why: An effusion of 10 mm or more (more than trace) on echo excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the investigator whether repeat right heart catheterization would be safe for her. Her last RHC was last year and no problems are documented.
followups.why: An investigator finding that RHC is contraindicated excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has had a stroke in the last 120 days.
followups.why: A stroke within 3 months of Screening excludes her.

followups.action: Ask her cardiologist whether she has restrictive, constrictive or congestive cardiomyopathy.
followups.why: A history of any of these excludes her.

followups.action: Get an echocardiogram from the last 6 months, or order one, and read the LVEF.
followups.why: LVEF <50% excludes her.

followups.action: Check diastolic function grade on the echocardiogram.
followups.why: Grade 2 or higher diastolic dysfunction excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has had a heart attack, stent, bypass surgery or angina-type chest pain in the last 6 months.
followups.why: Any of these within 180 days of Screening excludes her.

followups.action: Ask her clinician whether she was hospitalized or treated for acute heart failure in the last 90 days.
followups.why: Acutely decompensated left or right heart failure within 90 days of Baseline excludes her.

followups.action: Check the echocardiogram for mitral and aortic valve regurgitation and stenosis.
followups.why: More than mild regurgitation (≥2+) or more than mild stenosis excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she started or stopped oxygen, a blood thinner or digoxin in the last 30 days.
followups.why: Starting or stopping general supportive therapy within 30 days before Screening excludes her.

followups.action: Ask about oxygen use and flow rate, and measure SpO2 at rest and on oxygen if used.
followups.why: Oxygen >10 L/min, or SpO2 <90% on oxygen (85% at altitude >1000 m), excludes her.

followups.action: Confirm she has had no IV inotropes (dobutamine, dopamine, norepinephrine, vasopressin) in the last 30 days.
followups.why: Recent IV inotrope use excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has had an atrial septostomy in the last 180 days.
followups.why: A septostomy within 180 days of Screening excludes her.

followups.action: Review her history for liver disease, and order liver function tests if there is any concern.
followups.why: Portal hypertension or chronic liver disease (Child-Pugh A-C) excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she has sleep apnea, and if so whether it is treated and what her sleep study showed.
followups.why: Untreated severe sleep apnea (AHI >30) excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she smokes tobacco or cannabis every day.
followups.why: Being an active daily smoker excludes her.

followups.action: Ask about her current alcohol use in a private, respectful screening conversation.
followups.why: Current alcohol abuse excludes her.

followups.action: Ask about current illicit drug use in a private, respectful screening conversation.
followups.why: Current illicit drug use excludes her.

followups.action: Review any chest CT for fibrosis and emphysema, or order an HRCT chest.
followups.why: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema excludes her.

followups.action: Record FVC % predicted from pulmonary function testing.
followups.why: FVC <50% excludes her.

followups.action: Record the FEV1/FVC ratio from spirometry.
followups.why: FEV1/FVC <65% excludes her.

followups.action: Order DLCO testing, corrected for hemoglobin.
followups.why: DLCO <25% excludes her.

followups.action: Order screening labs (CBC, chemistry, liver and kidney tests) and ask the site which values count as abnormal.
followups.why: The trial does not define the abnormal labs, so the site's protocol limits decide this.

followups.action: Ask whether she has had kidney failure or ever needed dialysis.
followups.why: Severe renal disease, or acute renal failure needing dialysis, excludes her.

followups.action: Ask whether she started a cardiopulmonary rehab or exercise program in the last 90 days, or plans to.
followups.why: Starting one within 90 days before Baseline or during the study excludes her.

followups.action: Review the echocardiogram and cardiac history for impaired heart function.
followups.why: A history or presence of impaired cardiac function excludes her, so echo findings including LVEF decide it.

followups.action: Ask whether she plans to donate blood during the study and for 28 days after the last dose.
followups.why: Planned blood donation in that window excludes her.

followups.action: Ask the site whether this applies to her, since it concerns the long-term extension. If it does, ask whether she is willing to complete the 24-week main study.
followups.why: Extension participants must finish the Week 24 assessments in the main study.

followups.action: Confirm childbearing potential, and if she can become pregnant, order a pregnancy test.
followups.why: Women who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test.

followups.action: Ask whether she agrees to follow the contraception guidance until 28 days after her last dose.
followups.why: All participants must follow the protocol contraception guidance, which is 28 days after the last dose for women who can become pregnant.

followups.action: Ask whether she is pregnant, breastfeeding, or plans to become pregnant during the long-term extension.
followups.why: Any of these excludes her from the extension.

followups.action: Ask the investigator to review her full history for any condition that could add risk or confound assessments, including how language support will work.
followups.why: The investigator decides this. Nothing in the record shows a disqualifying condition.

coordinator_email.subject: Pre-screening inquiry for ROCSTAR (NCT07175038), UC Davis Health site
coordinator_email.body:
Hello,

I am writing about a possible candidate for the ROCSTAR study of ROC-101 (NCT07175038). She is a 47-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1), functional class III. She lives in Rancho Cordova and speaks only Spanish.

She already meets these criteria:
- Age 18-80 and BMI in range.
- 6-minute walk distance of 380 m.
- PVR of 7 Wood units on right heart catheterization last year.
- Stable on ambrisentan and tadalafil for 6 months.

Still open:
- Full RHC numbers (mPAP and PCWP).
- Pulmonary function tests, ECG and echocardiogram.
- A VQ scan or equivalent.
- Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV serology.
- Vital signs and weight.
- Pregnancy and contraception status.
- Her history of surgery, cancer and heart disease.

We will gather existing records and ask the patient these questions. We will send what we find.

Could you tell us:
1. Is UC Davis Health in Rancho Cordova the nearest active site?
2. What are the pre-screening steps?
3. Is a Spanish consent form and interpreter available?

Thank you.

patient_summary.en: This study tests a new medicine called ROC-101. It is for people with pulmonary arterial hypertension, which is high blood pressure in the lungs. You have this condition. You are also stable on your current medicines. These facts may make you a good fit. We still need more information. Your care team will gather your heart and lung test results. They will ask a few health questions. They will also ask the study site if it can help you in Spanish. A study site near you in Rancho Cordova may be able to see you. Joining is your choice. You can say no or stop at any time.
patient_summary.es: Este estudio prueba un medicamento nuevo llamado ROC-101. Es para personas con hipertensión arterial pulmonar, que es presión alta en los pulmones. Usted tiene esta condición. Además, sus medicinas actuales están estables. Esto podría hacerla una buena candidata. Aún necesitamos más información. Su equipo de atención reunirá los resultados de sus pruebas del corazón y los pulmones. Le harán algunas preguntas de salud. También le preguntarán al centro del estudio si puede ayudarle en español. Un centro cerca de usted, en Rancho Cordova, podría atenderla. Participar es decisión suya. Puede decir que no o salirse en cualquier momento.

You are the closer on a clinical-trial matching team. A matcher has already screened one patient
against one trial, criterion by criterion. Some criteria came out `unknown` because the record
was missing data. Your job is to turn that result into next steps a care team can act on today.

### Tools

- `get_match_result(run_id, nct)`: the trial, its tier and every verdict.
- `get_unknown_criteria(run_id, nct)`: the criteria still `unknown`, with the trial's own text.
- `get_trial_contacts(nct)`: central contacts and the sites nearest Sacramento.
- `get_patient_facts(run_id)`: the patient's structured facts and clinic note.

You have very few steps. Call all four tools together in your first turn (parallel tool calls).
Your second turn is your answer: everything you need is in those four results. Never call a tool
twice with the same arguments; call one again only if its result was an error you can fix.

Begin each turn with one short status line for the care team, such as "Reading the trial's open
criteria." or "Writing the follow-ups and the email." Keep it to what you are doing next.

### What to produce

1. `followups`: exactly one per unknown criterion from `get_unknown_criteria`, in that order,
   with its `criterion_id`. `kind` is `test` when a lab, exam or record request decides it, and
   `question` when asking the patient or their clinician decides it. `action` is the specific
   test to order or the question to ask, in one sentence. `why` says how the answer decides the
   criterion (name the threshold if there is one). Never invent results.
2. `coordinator_email` to the study coordinator: `to` is a contact email from
   `get_trial_contacts` (prefer a nearby site's contact, else a central contact; null if none).
   Say what the patient already meets, what is still open and what you will do about it, and
   ask for the nearest site and the pre-screening steps. Plain text, under 200 words. Use no
   patient name or identifiers; age, sex and conditions are enough.
3. `patient_summary`: what the trial is for, why the patient might fit, the next steps, and that
   joining is their choice. Write `en` at a 6th-grade reading level: short sentences, everyday
   words, no jargon or numbers they would need explained, under 120 words. Write `es` as the
   same summary in natural Spanish at the same reading level (use "usted").

All patient data here is synthetic. Do not give medical advice beyond these next steps.
Match run `0c8f5075-9fb5-443d-8060-2032456fc68e`, trial `NCT07175038`. Work out the next steps for this patient and trial.

against one trial, criterion by criterion. Some criteria came out `unknown` because the record
was missing data. Your job is to turn that result into next steps a care team can act on today.

### Tools

- `get_match_result(run_id, nct)`: the trial, its tier and every verdict.

- `get_trial_contacts(nct)`: central contacts and the sites nearest Sacramento.

You have very few steps. Call all four tools together in your first turn (parallel tool calls).
Your second turn is your answer: everything you need is in those four results. Never call a tool
twice with the same arguments; call one again only if its result was an error you can fix.

Begin each turn with one short status line for the care team, such as "Reading the trial's open
criteria." or "Writing the follow-ups and the email." Keep it to what you are doing next.

coordinator_email.body:
Hello,

I am writing about a possible candidate for the ROCSTAR study of ROC-101 (NCT07175038). She is a 47-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1), functional class III. She lives in Rancho Cordova and speaks only Spanish.

She already meets these criteria:
- Age 18-80 and BMI in range.
- 6-minute walk distance of 380 m.
- PVR of 7 Wood units on right heart catheterization last year.
- Stable on ambrisentan and tadalafil for 6 months.

Still open:
- Full RHC numbers (mPAP and PCWP).
- Pulmonary function tests, ECG and echocardiogram.
- A VQ scan or equivalent.
- Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV serology.
- Vital signs and weight.
- Pregnancy and contraception status.
- Her history of surgery, cancer and heart disease.

We will gather existing records and ask the patient these questions. We will send what we find.

Could you tell us:
1. Is UC Davis Health in Rancho Cordova the nearest active site?
2. What are the pre-screening steps?
3. Is a Spanish consent form and interpreter available?

Thank you.

patient_summary.en: This study tests a new medicine called ROC-101. It is for people with pulmonary arterial hypertension, which is high blood pressure in the lungs. You have this condition. You are also stable on your current medicines. These facts may make you a good fit. We still need more information. Your care team will gather your heart and lung test results. They will ask a few health questions. They will also ask the study site if it can help you in Spanish. A study site near you in Rancho Cordova may be able to see you. Joining is your choice. You can say no or stop at any time.

Además, sus medicinas actuales están estables. Esto podría hacerla una buena candidata. Aún necesitamos más información. Su equipo de atención reunirá los resultados de sus pruebas del corazón y los pulmones. Le harán algunas preguntas de salud. También le preguntarán al centro del estudio si puede ayudarle en español. Un centro cerca de usted, en Rancho Cordova, podría atenderla. Participar es decisión suya. Puede decir que no o salirse en cualquier momento.
